reports.title: FP16 MoE scratch capacity across two causal prefill chunks
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: Answers the supplied, current-source capacity/lifetime/order question, stays distinct from the R701/R702 generic grouped-GEMM and superchunk surveys, and makes no performance or adoption claim. The report is substantive and appropriately distinguishes payload capacity from the whole live path.

budget_assessment.scope_budget: pass; substantive body is within the 1,300-1,700 word working budget

reports.source_accuracy: The supplied thirteen source hashes match the plan, and the disclosed additional layer_major.inc hash matches the report. The source-backed capacity arithmetic, native16 BF16/FP16 distinction, route order, and publication limits are consistent with those inputs. A separate cited source path is outside the declared pin set and requires a localized hold as recorded below.

source_checks.source: Pinned Strata SYCL source set at 16f9eefa216f9f6d2f1fd5c18980612e7d6b656a
source_checks.verified: All thirteen path hashes in the plan match the shared worktree. The report's disclosed src/prefill/layer_major.inc SHA256 also matches. Core Dm payload capacity is exactly equal to two 8,192-row, top-10, two-byte planes; report correctly says this does not establish whole-window safety.

source_checks.source: src/prefill/sycl/gemm.cpp:102-106, cited in R871 but absent from the source pin list
source_checks.verified: The citation is not among the thirteen pinned paths or the sole disclosed additional file. No hash or justification appears in the report, although the pre-dispatch refinement required pinning every additional source before use. The review does not rely on this unpinned implementation detail.

corrections.correction: R871 cites src/prefill/sycl/gemm.cpp:102-106 to establish the non-native16 Gemm::f16 output type, but reports only the thirteen supplied hashes plus src/prefill/layer_major.inc as read. The cited gemm.cpp path and SHA256 are absent. Hold that clause until its source pin and permitted-use basis are reconciled; the pinned native16 output-format and Dm-capacity findings remain usable with this caveat.

nonblocking_review_notes: The report correctly keeps FP16/BF16 format choice, numerical quality, performance, and default adoption as separate open gates; the old nonexclusive unitrace totals are not used as a MoE speed claim.
The extra layer_major.inc disclosure satisfies the pre-dispatch refinement by giving its hash and using it to establish caller order/publication boundaries.

sections: 7-12: Dm two-chunk payload extent and current FP32/BF16/FP16 output-format distinctions; apply R871-C1 to the gemm.cpp clause on line 9.
15-28: allocator guards, exact per-plane capacities and live intervals, routes/shared/state buffers, and phase-overlay accounting.
26-28: total routed-row count, per-expert bound, slot-order combine, and MoE/QSA/GDN shared-region lifetime.
32-36: serialized reuse versus deferred window, causal operator order, callbacks/checkpoints, layer publication, and peer/MMQ/compact-mode limits.
40: decision boundary and independent numerical, performance, format, and adoption gates.
keys: BF16 native16 output versus FP32 fallback and FP16 scratch
preserve_caveats: R871-C1: src/prefill/sycl/gemm.cpp was not pinned in the report; do not rely on that cited non-native16 output-type clause until reconciled.
The exact two-byte Dm fit is a payload-capacity result, not proof that route maps, shared inputs, residuals, and callbacks support a live two-chunk window.
The report is static source analysis and establishes no speed, quality, or adoption result.

reports.title: GPU equijoin build/probe crossovers under key skew and memory limits
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: Answers the assigned single-GPU equijoin crossover question with direct hash, partitioned hash, and sort-merge evidence. It remains separate from R867's query-pipeline fusion boundary and does not make a Strata/Arc claim.
reports.source_accuracy: The report's cited primary sources support the source-specific results and the report preserves their differing devices, workloads, and timing boundaries. The narrow-join 4x, PHJ-OM materialization comparisons, match-ratio reversal, 2017 two-to-three-pass cliff and new two-pass design, and Awad hash-table probe counts match their cited primary papers.

source_checks.source: Wu, Koutsoukos, and Alonso, Efficiently Processing Large Relational Joins on GPUs, arXiv:2312.00720v1
source_checks.verified: The primary text reports the 4x narrow-join comparison, PHJ-OM's 2.3x/1.4x wide-join comparisons, the below-25% match-ratio reversal, 2^27-row allocation figures, A100/RTX 3090 settings, and seven-run medians while excluding most allocation/auxiliary initialization.
source_checks.scope_limit: The direct-hash crossover and skew evidence are from the paper's evaluated primary-foreign-key workloads; the report states they do not predict every table design or many-to-many hot-key case.

source_checks.source: Rui and Tu, Fast Equi-Join Algorithms on GPUs: Design and Implementation, SSDBM 2017
source_checks.verified: The source documents the 2017 two-pass partitioning design, its comparison with the older code's 32M two-to-three-pass jump, the 6GB Titan 128M limit, and sort-merge up to 26% faster than hash on the named Titan X/Titan tests.
source_checks.scope_limit: CUDA/NVIDIA historical measurements with the specific 32-bit key/payload and workload setup described in the report.

source_checks.source: He et al., Relational Joins on Graphics Processors
source_checks.verified: The report's G80-era row preserves the source's default 16M workload, transfer-inclusive timing, output count/scan/emit handling, and 1.3s hash versus 2.0s sort-merge figures.
source_checks.scope_limit: Historical 8800 GTX results, not a modern-GPU crossover.

source_checks.source: Awad et al., Better GPU Hash Tables, arXiv:2108.07232v3
source_checks.verified: The source supports 1.43 mean insertion probes and 2.8 negative-query probes at 0.99 load; the report labels these as table microbenchmarks rather than join evidence.
source_checks.scope_limit: Does not model duplicate payload lists, output, or end-to-end join allocation.

corrections.correction: The R872 plan and dispatched spec label arXiv:2312.00720v1 as 'Efficiently Processing Joins and Grouped Aggregations on GPUs.' The URL resolves to the original paper titled 'Efficiently Processing Large Relational Joins on GPUs.' R872 cites the actual title correctly, so this does not change a report finding; use the corrected title in future index metadata.

nonblocking_review_notes: The word count and four primary sources fit the assignment. The direct hash table evidence is properly separated from end-to-end join performance, and the report distinguishes key-frequency skew from partition occupancy.

keys: direct hash versus partitioned hash versus sort-merge phases
table load factor and output allocation
preserve_caveats: Cross-paper speedups are not controlled rankings.
A static GPU hash-table probe count is not an end-to-end join crossover.
R872's direct-hash results are dominated by primary-foreign-key evidence; do not generalize its skew behavior to arbitrary many-to-many hot keys.

reports.title: Stationary dataflows and array utilization in non-LLM inference ASICs
reports.scope_and_novelty_assessment: Answers the dense FC/MLP dataflow question at the ASIC-architecture level, separates historical measured TPU counters from analytical Eyeriss estimates, and stays distinct from earlier GPU convolution, kernel-geometry, and bank-layout collections.
reports.source_accuracy: The original Eyeriss, TPU v1, MAESTRO, Timeloop, and MAERI sources support the attributed mechanisms and evidence. Reported Eyeriss energy ratios are explicitly analytical; TPU counters and fabricated-chip specifications are kept separate.

source_checks.source: Chen, Emer, and Sze, Eyeriss, ISCA 2016
source_checks.verified: The paper's FC section gives the 16-bit, 1,024-PE AlexNet sweep, batch 1 weight-DRAM caveat, OSA small-spatial-extent limitation, and RS energy advantage from at least 1.3x at batch 16 to up to 2.8x at batch 256. The report labels these as model results and distinguishes the 168-PE fabricated Eyeriss chip.
source_checks.scope_limit: Model-derived FC cross-dataflow results are not measurements from the fabricated chip.

source_checks.source: Jouppi et al., In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit, ISCA 2017 v1
source_checks.verified: The source confirms the 256x256 8-bit matrix unit, 4 MiB accumulator, 24 MiB unified buffer, 64 KiB double-buffered weight tiles, documented Bx256-by-256x256 instruction, MLP weights/batches, and MLP active/useful/weight-stall counters quoted in R873.
source_checks.scope_limit: Production app counters do not provide individual MLP matrix shapes or isolate one cause for all inactive cycles; the report says so.

source_checks.source: Kwon et al., MAESTRO; Parashar et al., Timeloop; Kwon, Samajdar, and Krishna, MAERI
source_checks.verified: These primary sources support the model/directive/mapspace and configurable multicast/reduction-fabric descriptions. The report does not use MAERI's heterogeneous utilization headline as an FC number.
source_checks.scope_limit: Architecture models and flexible-fabric examples are not measured desktop-GPU or product results.

nonblocking_review_notes: The traffic and tile-capacity equations are clearly marked as derived accounting models, not measured ASIC results. The calculated 112 MiB comparison applies to the FC weight set and 512 KiB reference buffer in the stated Eyeriss analysis.

keys: partial-sum traffic and local storage model
Eyeriss modeled FC comparisons and limits
TPU v1 MLP array activity and stalls
preserve_caveats: Eyeriss FC energy ratios are analytical model results, separate from the fabricated chip's specifications.
TPU v1 MLP evidence is 2017 production workload data; individual layer shapes are not reported.
No ASIC result establishes a desktop SYCL/GPU performance prediction.
